title: Michigan Residents Voted to Get Corporate Money Out of Politics. Now Utilities Are Suing
gist: Michigan voters passed Proposal 2 with 81% support, banning political donations from utilities, large state contractors, their executives and families; Consumers Energy and DTE have sued on First and 14th Amendment grounds. The fight sits atop a data-center buildout, rising power bills and DTE's proposed $6.4 billion gas plants, signaling a national utility-accountability wave.

insights.claim: Michigan's Proposal 2, passed with 81 percent of the vote, bans political donations from utilities, companies with over $250,000 a year in state and local government contracts, and their high-level employees, lobbyists and immediate family members, and tightens political-ad disclosure rules.
insights.speaker: Molly Taft
insights.so_what: Removes a key political-influence channel for regulated utilities in a major data-center state.
